newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo welcomes UN move on massacre probe.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo welcomes UN move on massacre probe.

text.p: President Laurent Kabila's government on Wednesday welcomed a U.N. decision to send a new investigation team to look into allegations that his forces or their Tutsi allies massacred Rwandan Hutu refugees.
But it stood by a demand that the inquiry be widened to include any incidents dating back to 1993 and not just during its seven-month rebellion that toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May.
Information Minister and government spokesman Raphael Ghenda welcomed the move as a "positive development" but said that the question was whether the investigators would be impartial.
"It's a step forward. I think the (U.N.) Secretary-General understood our concern. We wanted to make sure that the investigators would be impartial," Ghenda told Reuters.
"Most of the time, what happens is that the accusers become themselves the investigators," he said.

Kabila, who has denied the allegations, opposed any investigation by Chilean Roberto Garreton, the U.N. Special Rapporteur for human rights, who has already accused his forces of massacring refugees in their march across Zaire, now renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Ghenda said Kinshasa still wanted an investigation back to 1993. "We haven't changed our minds as for the time period. It's a reasonable period. We also want the investigation to look into what happened before we came to power in May," Ghenda said.

Over a million Hutus crossed into what was then Zaire fearing reprisals for the 1994 genocide in Rwanda of minority Tutsis by Hutu hardliners. The bulk returned home but relief officials say up to 200,000 remain unaccounted for.
